checks: No eclipse at 1 of 7 covered epochs where the 2.54512 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 237657109 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.5451 days. The system shows a primary eclipse that dims the star by 1.55 percent, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 56.3 in automated photometry. Pixel-level analysis confirms the eclipse signature with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 21.1, though the centroid offset of 7.2 arcsec from the target warrants further investigation. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a newly identified candidate. The pipeline's machine-learning model assigned it a likelihood score of 0.32, reflecting moderate confidence in its status as a real target. This candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
